notes.claim: A buck converter takes its input from a DC source such as a battery, switching it through a transistor into a diode, inductor and capacitor.
In a buck converter's steady state the volt-second balance is (Vin - Vo) times Ton equals Vo times Toff, so Vo is Vin times the share of time on.
A boost converter steps a voltage up by storing energy in an inductor and releasing it to the load at a higher voltage.
In a boost converter, when the switch is on the inductor voltage is about the input voltage and energy is stored in the inductor.
A switching supply is more efficient than a linear one, and can step a voltage up, step it down or invert it.
In a converter's steady state the average voltage across the inductor is zero.
When a buck converter's switch opens, the inductor current keeps flowing through the diode and charges the output.
A good first estimate for a buck converter's inductor ripple current is 20% to 40% of the output current.
For i6: on a ship's DC distribution, power sources can join the DC bus directly or through converters such as DC/DC converters.
